REGULATION (EU) 2099/1 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL

of 1 January 2099

laying down harmonised rules on fixture systems and amending Regulation (EU) 2016/679

(Text with EEA relevance)

THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,

Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Articles 16 and 114 thereof,

Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee (1),

Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure (2),

Whereas:

(1)

The purpose of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market by laying down a uniform legal framework for fixture systems, in accordance with Union values.

(2)

Fixture systems can be easily deployed in a large variety of sectors of the economy. This Regulation should therefore be applied consistently across the Union.

(3)

In order to ensure a high level of protection, the following elements should be considered:

(a)

the safety of natural persons;

(b)

the protection of fundamental rights.

HAVE ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

Subject matter

1. The purpose of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market and promote the uptake of trustworthy fixture systems.

2. This Regulation lays down:

(a)

harmonised rules for the placing on the market of fixture systems;

(b)

prohibitions of certain practices, including:

(i)

manipulative techniques;

(ii)

exploitative techniques.

Article 2

Scope

1. This Regulation shall apply to providers placing fixture systems on the market, irrespective of whether those providers are established in the Union or in a third country.

2. This Regulation does not apply to areas outside the scope of Union law.

Article 5 shall not apply to systems developed exclusively for scientific research.

CHAPTER II

FINAL PROVISIONS

Article 3

Entry into force

This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

Done at Brussels, 1 January 2099.

For the European Parliament

The President
